paragraphs: Farmer John is yet again trying to take a photograph of his N cows (2 ≤ N ≤ 1000).

Each cow has an integer "breed ID" number in the range 1…100. Farmer John has a very peculiar idea in mind for his photo: he wants to partition all the cows into disjoint groups (in other words, place each cow in exactly one group) and then line up the groups so the sum of the breed IDs of the cows in the first group is even, the sum of the IDs in the second group is odd, and so on, alternating between even and odd.
What is the maximum possible number of groups Farmer John can form?
inputFormat: The first line of input contains N.
The next line contains N space-separated integers giving the breed IDs of the N cows.
outputFormat: Print the maximum possible number of groups in Farmer John's photo. It can be shown that at least one feasible grouping exists.

additionalSamples.explanation: 1 even cow and 6 odd cows: pair up two odds twice to have 3 even groups and 2 odd groups → 5 alternating groups: [2], [11], [13, 1], [15], [17, 3].

sampleExplanation.detail: All 7 cows have odd IDs. One way to form 3 alternating groups (Even, Odd, Even) is [1, 3], [5, 7, 9], [11, 13].

hints.title: Only Parity Matters!
hints.body: The exact breed ID doesn't matter — only whether each cow is even (0) or odd (1)! Count E = number of even cows and O = number of odd cows.

hints.title: What If There Are Too Many Evens?
hints.body: In an alternating sequence Even, Odd, Even, Odd, …, the number of Even groups is either equal to Odd groups or Odd + 1. Since adding an even number to any group doesn't change its parity, extra evens beyond O + 1 can just be absorbed: E = min(E, O + 1).

hints.title: What If There Are Too Many Odds?
hints.body: Two odd cows can be paired together to form ONE even-sum group (odd + odd = even)! So while O > E, convert two odds into one even: O -= 2, E += 1. Afterward, apply E = min(E, O + 1), and the answer is E + O!

editorial.summary: Count even cows (E) and odd cows (O). While O > E, pair two odd cows into a single even group (O −= 2, E += 1). Then cap E = min(E, O + 1) by merging any surplus even cows into existing groups without changing parity. Output E + O.

solutions.python:
import sys

def solve():
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
    n = data[0]
    even = sum(1 for x in data[1:1 + n] if x % 2 == 0)
    odd = n - even
    while odd > even:
        odd -= 2
        even += 1
    if even > odd + 1:
        even = odd + 1
    print(even + odd)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
